text.p: Cyprus shares were pushed up in mid-week trading with a rally on banking shares which started on Monday, traders said.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index closed at 82.41 on Wednesday, gaining 1.60 percent from its close of 81.12 on Friday.
The market opened with a hiccup on Monday when the board of the exchange suspended trading in two cement stocks for issuing contradictory statements on the floor about share transactions.
Trading in Vassiliko Cement Works and Cyprus Cement was halted for two days after the first company announced a deal to buy a huge block of shares in the other which the second disputed.
Both companies were back trading on Wednesday. "The investor has the picture at his disposal, it is up to him to decide," CSE director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters.
Vassiliko shares closed at 173.5, an 8 percent rise over its last trading day on Friday where the share closed at 160.5. Cyprus cement was up half a cent at 265.5.
Banking shares rose 1.6 percent, closing at 90.65 from 89.21 on Friday.
Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed at 343, up 9.5 cents from Friday.
"The week opened with a rally on Bank of Cyprus shares with different brokers buying," said Stavros Agrotis from CISCO. "There is no particular reason. They think it is a good share to buy."
Fully paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank gained two cents, closing at 323.5.
The Hellenic Bank closed at 260, down half a cent from Friday. Shares in the Universal Savings Bank shed one cent, closing at 138.
The insurance stock index fell to 57.17 from 57.57 last week.
Universal Life shares gained 1.5 cents, closing at 379.5. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid closed at 124.5, down one cent from Friday.
Interamerican Insurance fully paid closed up one cent at 100.5. Philiki Insurance fully paid declined 8.5 cents, closing at 224.
Beer and wine producers Keo, gained five cents, closing at 114.
National carrier Cyprus Airways was trading at 38.6 cents from 39.3 on Friday.
